explain: A cascaded voice pipeline has separate recognition, agent, and synthesis stages. These injected functions use symbolic bytes and are not real audio engines.
steps: Turn a synthetic audio fixture into text. || Pass text through the agent and synthesize a symbolic response to expose the stage boundaries.
name: voice-pipeline

explain: Partial recognition hypotheses can be revised and must not trigger irreversible effects. The final utterance is kept under a stable identity and revision.
steps: Replace the earlier hypothesis with the newer transcript. || Allow only finalized intent to reach the sensitive-action check.
name: partial-transcript

explain: Silence thresholds affect responsiveness and premature endpointing. A timeout is a turn-detection heuristic, not evidence that the speaker intended an action.
steps: Compare observed silence with the configured threshold. || Show how changing the threshold changes the turn-end decision on the same sample.
name: turn-detection

explain: Interruption changes the active generation and rejects late audio from the old one. Stopping playback and cancelling generation are separate operations in a real client.
steps: Increment the active generation on interruption. || Filter queued audio frames by that identity before playback.
name: barge-in

explain: Recognition confidence does not establish authorization or exact confirmation. A sensitive action requires a verified principal and an approved current parameter set.
steps: Keep ASR confidence separate from review state. || Require all trusted action prerequisites before committing.
name: voice-confirmation

explain: Audio and transcript retention are separate product decisions, and text fallback supports users who cannot or do not want to speak. This is a policy fixture, not a legal compliance assertion.
steps: Explicitly disable raw-audio retention for this scenario. || Preserve a text interaction path when microphone access is unavailable.
name: audio-privacy

explain: Uncompressed PCM bytes depend on sample rate, channels, and bit depth. Codec compression and network overhead are outside this calculation.
steps: Convert bit depth to bytes per sample. || Calculate one second and one 20 ms frame with the same declared format.
name: audio-size

explain: Voice evaluation includes final intent, interruption recovery, and first audible response. A correct transcript alone does not establish a successful conversation.
steps: Define separate checks for recognition, intent, and playback recovery. || Fail the task when a late generation remains audible despite correct text.
name: voice-evaluation
